findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password check whenever a totpCode is also posted, so a valid backup code alone authenticates
findings.description: The password check at line 121 only runs when `!credentials.totpCode`. The new backup-code branch at line 131 has no password check of its own. A POST to the credentials callback with any non-empty `totpCode`, a valid `backupCode`, and a wrong `password` skips `verifyPassword`. Line 131 then accepts the backup code, and the function returns the user. The UI never sends both fields, because "Lost access" clears `totpCode` (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:125), but `authorize` trusts the posted body. The result is that email plus one backup code is enough to log in, and the password factor is gone. The existing TOTP branch has the same gate, so the bypass already exists for TOTP. This change adds a second factor that uses it. The fix is to verify the password whenever `user.password` is set for a CAL identity, independent of `totpCode`. `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:40-45` already does this correctly.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is an unlocked read-modify-write, so concurrent logins can replay a consumed code
findings.description: `user.backupCodes` is read at line 89 in the select. The code decrypts it, sets `backupCodes[index] = null` at line 148, and writes the whole blob back at lines 149-156. There is no compare-and-set and no transaction. Two concurrent requests with the same valid code both pass the `indexOf` at line 144 and both log in. Two requests with different codes, c1 and c2, both read `[c1..c10]`. The later write then restores c1, so a consumed code becomes valid again. A fix is a conditional update keyed on the originally read ciphertext, failing when the count is 0, or a transaction with a row lock.

findings.title: Dismissing the enable dialog with X or Escape on the backup-codes step never calls onEnable, so the page keeps showing 2FA as disabled
findings.description: The server enables 2FA on success, and then the modal moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` (line 135). `onEnable` runs only from the Close button (lines 266-270). The Dialog forwards X and Escape to `onOpenChange` (packages/ui/components/dialog/Dialog.tsx:39-41). The settings page maps that to a plain toggle (apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64) that does not invalidate `viewer.me`. Until the next refetch, the Switch (`checked={user?.twoFactorEnabled}`, line 46) and the "Disabled" badge show the old state while the account has 2FA on. The codes are only shown in this step, so this path also lets users skip the save, copy, and download step without any signal.

findings.title: Passing type="password" to PasswordField overrides its visibility toggle, so the eye button never reveals the password in the enable dialog
findings.description: `PasswordField` computes `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` at packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:36, then spreads `{...props}` at line 39. The caller's `type="password"` at EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:176 overwrites the computed value. The button's icon and tooltip flip, but the input stays masked. The other callers do not pass `type` (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:203-209 and apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:94), and their toggles work. Removing the prop fixes this.

findings.title: tabIndex={-1} on the PasswordField visibility toggle removes it from keyboard navigation for every password field
findings.description: The `tabIndex={-1}` at line 49 applies to every `PasswordField` in the app, including login, the reset form, and both 2FA modals. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach the reveal control with Tab. Nothing in the diff explains or compensates for this. The default tab order should be restored, or the change should be justified and the control kept reachable.

findings.title: Lost-access recovery for accounts that enabled 2FA before this change shows a message telling them to regenerate codes, which the app does not allow
findings.description: Line 137 throws `MissingBackupCodes` when `user.backupCodes` is null. The migration (packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql) adds the column with no backfill, so accounts that enabled 2FA earlier have null codes. The message at apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json:2019 says "Please generate them in your settings." However, `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:42-44` returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` for any account with `twoFactorEnabled` true, and the settings page only offers enable and disable. Those users cannot use the recovery path, and they cannot regenerate codes either, because disabling 2FA requires a TOTP code or a backup code. The fix is a backfill or a regenerate path, and a corrected message either way.

findings.title: Submitting the login Lost-access form with an empty backup code shows no error
findings.description: The login form is `noValidate` (line 188), so the `required` attribute on `BackupCode` is not enforced. An empty `backupCode` is posted. In `authorize`, the falsy value skips the branch at next-auth-options.ts:131, and lines 158-159 throw `SecondFactorRequired`. The handler at line 156 only calls `setTwoFactorRequired(true)`, which is already true, so `errorMessage` stays null and nothing visible happens. The fix is to show an error when `twoFactorLostAccess` is set and the code is empty.
